chift_routes.one_line: Map to POST /invoices.sales.new (customer_*) or POST /invoices.purchases.new (supplier_*), with Type 0 for an invoice and 1 for a credit note, using multipart/form-data when a PDF is attached. First resolve FolderId (D7), the DaybookId per invoice_type with the refund fallback 250→200 / 150→100 (D1), a found-or-created CompanyId (partner_info: lookup by external reference, then by the exact code with a name check, otherwise create; proposal, D10), the account search keys, and the cost schema/section search keys from the per-folder analytics cache (D8). Main caveats: Horus has no VAT-code list or VAT-code input, so tax_code is decoded from the connector's catalogue (S-…/P-… grammar, D2), built from the Horus tax-combination files per folder legislation and direction; Number must be numeric, with no auto-numbering (an invoice without a number is pushed unconfirmed and returned as draft, proposal, C7), no idempotency key and no invoice delete (best-effort DocumentNo pre-check, D12); Confirmed follows the per-connection posting mode (D12, proposal, C1); reference and customer_memo share the header Comment (D3). Horus returns only the book entry Id, so the response is rebuilt from the echo plus GET /book-entries.info (folder-checked, D13), and POST /account-histories.list only when line-level data is needed (EUR amounts, D4).

summary:
Horus has two native write endpoints for this route. POST /invoices.sales.new takes customer_invoice (Type=0) and customer_refund (Type=1). POST /invoices.purchases.new takes supplier_invoice (Type=0) and supplier_refund (Type=1). Both accept header totals, VAT-qualified lines, multi-schema cost lines, a currency and the PDF in one multipart call. Horus's own posting guide lists the four prerequisites the connector must resolve first: FolderId, a 200/250 or 100/150 DaybookId, a found-or-created CompanyId, and the account search keys.

One Chift call therefore becomes several Horus calls:
- **Folder (D7):** folder_id is required when the connection has more than one selected folder; otherwise the single selected folder, or the single folder from folders.list, is used.
- **Cached lookups per folder:** daybooks (D1 filter: customer_invoice → 200; customer_refund → 250, else 200; supplier_invoice → 100; supplier_refund → 150, else 100; exactly one candidate or 400 'journal_id required'), accounts, the analytics cache (cost schemas + cost sections including inactive ones, D8), fiscal-year bounds, and the folder (Legislation, IsVatLiable, WithAnalytics). Closure dates are read fresh before each create, because the accountant can close a period at any time.
- **Partner:** partner_id is folder-checked with companies.info (D13). partner_info (proposal, D10, C8): companies.list by ExternalReference, then by the exact SearchKey as sent (a code that sanitising would change is rejected); a match is reused only if its name matches account_name; a missing customer/supplier role is reported (422) unless Chift enables the flag update; otherwise companies.new. Partner writes run only after every other check has passed.
- **Duplicate pre-check (D12, best effort):** book-entries.list on DocumentNo whenever invoice_number is supplied, and again before any retry; supplier invoices without a number get a supplier + date + total check (proposal). Horus documents no uniqueness or idempotency key and offers no invoice delete, so a create without a number is never retried automatically.
- **The create call itself.**
- **Read-back (skipped when ignore_accounting_id=true):** create returns only {Id}, so GET /book-entries.info?Id=… reads the entry back in one call with no period and its Folder.Id is checked (D13). POST /account-histories.list filtered on BookEntryId is added only when line-level data is needed (the EUR partner-line amount of a foreign-currency invoice per D4, the partner collective account).

The biggest risk is VAT. Chift sends tax_code as 'the Id of the Tax Code', but Horus has no VAT-code list and accepts no VAT code on write. Each line needs TaxRate + TaxOrigin + TaxType (purchases add TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue), and the valid combinations are published by Horus in the two spreadsheets linked from the invoice endpoints (downloaded 13 Oct 2026, appendix C), one list per legislation (BE, LU) and direction. The connector therefore owns a VAT-code catalogue per folder legislation and direction, with one canonical id grammar shared with GET vat-codes and get_invoices (D2): 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}' (+ '-{TaxCountryCode}' for OSS) and 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}'. The LU files use TaxOrigin codes outside the enums of the API reference, so codes are validated against the files, and Horus must confirm which source is authoritative (H1). VAT amounts are booked as sent (OverrideTaxAmounts=true, proposed decision 'VAT amounts as issued', C2).

Other risks:
- Per-plan percentages must become joint cost-line amounts (maximum 8 schemas), rounded with the largest-remainder method; Free schemas are excluded in v1 (D8).
- invoice_number must be numeric (no leading zeros, at most 15 digits). Horus cannot generate a missing invoice number: such an invoice is pushed unconfirmed with Number 0 and returned as draft (proposal, C7).
- API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them. Confirmed follows the per-connection posting mode (D12, proposal, C1): review mode, the proposed default, pushes every invoice unconfirmed; direct mode confirms 'posted' invoices. The response reports the status actually stored.
- Credit notes may fall back to a 200/100 daybook (D1), which Horus has not confirmed it accepts.
- Amount signs follow one document-level policy (proposal, C5, H2): a refund with negative totals is sign-flipped as a whole; negative invoices and negative lines are rejected until Horus confirms they are accepted.
- reference and customer_memo share the header Comment ('{reference} | {customer_memo}', D3), so reference is lost as a structured field.
- Several Chift fields have no Horus field: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, start/end/delivery dates, force_financial_period, payment_term_id, and line quantity/unit price. They are rejected with 422 or ignored and logged, because the create response has no warnings field (C3).

Operationally, every retry must first run the duplicate pre-check, token refreshes must be serialised (refresh tokens are single-use), and all write tests must use a test folder, because the API works on the license's real data.
verdict_rationale:
The capability is native. Horus has dedicated sale and purchase invoice endpoints with credit-note support, lines, VAT, multi-axis analytics, currency and the PDF in one call, and the Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices describes exactly this use case. Under the shared verdict calibration (D11: workaround = feasible, but needs extra per-request calls, emulated behaviour, or loses capabilities clients rely on), the verdict is workaround, not supported, for six reasons:
1. The required Chift tax_code has no Horus counterpart. A combination of enums must be emulated from a connector-maintained catalogue with the D2 id grammar, built from the Horus tax-combination files per folder legislation and direction.
2. Every reference must be resolved or validated through other endpoints: folder (D7), daybook per invoice_type with the refund fallback (D1), partner found (with a name check) or created (D10) and folder-checked (D13), accounts, and cost schemas/sections from the per-folder cache (D8). Analytics must be converted from percentages to amounts.
3. Numbering and idempotency need an emulated, best-effort pre-check through book-entries.list (D12). Horus has no AutoGenerateNumber on invoices, no documented uniqueness rule, and no invoice delete to undo a duplicate.
4. The Chift response must be rebuilt from echoed values plus read-back calls, because create returns only {Id}. GET /book-entries.info reads the header back in one call by Id, but line-level data (EUR amounts under D4, partner collective account, booked VAT and cost detail) still needs the period-bounded account-histories.list.
5. Several Chift fields are lost or rejected: reference as a structured field (merged into Comment, D3), withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, accrual and delivery dates, force_financial_period, payment_term_id, quantity/unit_price/unit_of_measure, and Free-schema analytics (D8).
6. Status mapping has business weight: Horus API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, hence the proposed per-connection posting mode, review by default (D12).

call_sequence: 0. Connection context (Chift-internal). consumer_id → the stored Horus connection: one per license, holding api_url, access token, refresh token and expiry. Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh proactively a few minutes before expiry, under a per-connection lock, and persist the new token pair before using it, because refresh tokens are single-use (Guide: Token lifecycle). Send Content-Encoding: gzip (Guide: Making requests) and ignore unknown response properties (Guide: Changes & versioning). FolderId (D7): folder_id when given (rejected with 400 'folder not selected for this connection' if it is not in the activation selection); if it is null and exactly one folder was selected at activation, that folder; if no selection is stored, the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0}; otherwise 400 'folder_id required'.

1. Chift-side validation, before any Horus call:
- total = untaxed_amount + tax_amount on the header and on each line.
- Amounts carry at most 2 decimals; otherwise 422, or round half-up to the cent and route any header residue through invoice_correction, per Chift's choice (C3). All equality checks use decimal arithmetic on cent values (no floating point).
- Sign rule (proposal, C5, H2): a refund whose header total is below 0 is multiplied by −1 as a whole (header, lines, correction). An invoice (not a refund) with a negative total, and a line whose sign is opposite to the document, are rejected with 422 until Horus confirms that negative amounts are accepted.
- Header totals = sum of the lines within the rounding tolerance agreed with Chift (invoice_correction, proposal); a larger difference, or any difference without invoice_correction → 422.
- Optional per-consumer plausibility check (proposal, off by default): |tax_amount − untaxed_amount × tax_rate / 100| within an agreed tolerance on each line, otherwise 422.
- Analytic percentages are integers summing to 100 per plan, with at most 8 plans.
- Every tax_code (and correction tax code) carries the prefix of the invoice side (S- for customer_*, P- for supplier_*); membership of the folder's list is checked in step 5.
- The PDF type is one of Pdf/Xml/CODA/SODA/jpg/jpeg/png.
- Reject with 422: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, a force_financial_period that differs from the invoice_date month, a delivery_date in another month if Chift chooses rejection (C3), a currency outside the Horus enum, and an invoice_number that is non-numeric, has leading zeros, more than 15 digits, or equals 0.
2. If regroup_lines='true' (the default), merge lines that share (account_number, tax_code, analytic_distribution), summing untaxed_amount, tax_amount and total.

3. Reference data, loaded once and cached per folder (Guide: Reading accounting data):
- POST /daybooks.list: resolve DaybookId with the D1 filter (customer_invoice [200]; customer_refund [250], else [200]; supplier_invoice [100]; supplier_refund [150], else [100]); exactly one candidate, otherwise 400 'journal_id required'. A given journal_id must be in this folder-scoped list with a Type of the invoice side.
- POST /accounts.list: exact search key, Inactive=false, optionally IsSummary=false.
- Analytics cache (D8): POST /cost-schemas.list, then POST /cost-sections.list per List-type schema with Filter.IncludeInactive = true. Map GUID ids to search keys; read Mandatory and CostSectionType.
- Closure check, fresh for every create (not from the long-lived cache): POST /fiscal-years.list {FolderId, Filter:{Dates:[invoice_date], IncludeFuture:true}} → bounds and closure dates; GET /fiscal-years.info for IsClosed (a year already closed may be cached). Horus recommends this check (Guide: Data model); the accountant can close a period at any time, so at most a short TTL (minutes), refreshed after any Horus 400 on a write, is acceptable.
- GET /folders.info: WithAnalytics, Language, CountryCode, Legislation (BE or LU: selects the tax-combination list used in step 5) and IsVatLiable.

4. Partner (Guide: Managing customers & suppliers: 'find or create the company first'). Only lookups run here; a partner write (companies.new, or the opt-in companies.update) runs after steps 5 to 7 have passed, just before step 8.
- partner_id set: CompanyId = partner_id. Guard with GET /companies.info (cached): Data.Folder.Id must equal folder_id, otherwise 400 (D13); check IsCustomer/IsSupplier for the invoice side; a missing flag → 422 (or the opt-in flag update).
- partner_id null and partner_info set (proposal, D10, C8): POST /companies.list (FolderId, Filter.ExternalReference = account_number as sent), exact same-folder post-filter (string filters are 'contains'); if none, Filter.SearchKey = account_number as sent, exact same-folder post-filter. The code is never sanitised or truncated: a code that breaks create_client's SearchKey rules (H7) is rejected with 422. Reuse on a match is intended here because the key is the consumer's own code, whereas create_client derives its key from the name. On a match, check the name against account_name: 409 with the existing id on a mismatch, or reuse with a logged warning, per C8. A missing IsCustomer/IsSupplier flag → 422, or POST /companies.update with CompanyId + that flag only (never "" values) when Chift enables it. If no match, POST /companies.new with create_client's required-field rules (SearchKey = account_number, LanguageCode = folder Language per D9, CountryCode = folder CountryCode, IsVatLiable=false, ExternalReference = account_number if C8 confirms a third-party code), and use the returned Id as CompanyId.
- Both null: reject with 422, because CompanyId is required.

5. VAT (D2): decode each lines[].tax_code, and the correction tax code, through the connector's catalogue for the folder's Legislation and the invoice direction (sales list for customer_*, purchase list for supplier_*), built from the Horus tax-combination files (appendix C; sales BE 18 rows, LU 58; purchases BE 109, LU 146).
- Sales 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}' → TaxRate, TaxOrigin, TaxType; OSS rows (BE TaxOrigin 13; LU TaxOrigin 24, 26, 29) carry a fifth component → TaxCountryCode, and their rate is supplied per transaction ('XX' in the files).
- Purchases 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}' → the six fields, 'x' → null; on LU rows with TaxCondition 0 (COUNTRY) the condition value is the country code.
An id that is not in the folder's list for the invoice direction → 422 'tax_code not valid for this folder'. Check the decoded rate against lines[].tax_rate. TaxOrigin is validated against the files, not against the reference enum, which does not contain the LU codes (H1).

6. Numbering and duplicate pre-check (D12, best effort). invoice_number must be numeric, without leading zeros, at most 15 digits and not 0, otherwise 422 (same rule as miscellaneous operations); Number = int(invoice_number).
- invoice_number set: POST /book-entries.list (FolderId, DaybookId, fiscal-year months, Filter.DocumentNo=Number) before creating. Unconfirmed entries are included by default. If an entry exists, return 409 Conflict (or the existing entry, per Chift policy, C6). This follows Horus's advice to reconcile on daybook + entry number.
- invoice_number null (proposal, Chift decision C7): push the invoice unconfirmed with Number=0 ('can be 0 if not confirmed', documented on both endpoints) and return status 'draft' with invoice_number null, in both posting modes (D12). How Horus numbers it when the accountant confirms it is undocumented (H3). Alternatives per connection: reject with 422 'invoice_number is required for posted invoices on Horus', or, opt-in only and once Horus confirms that numbers are unique and enforced (H3), Number = max(DocumentNo)+1 per daybook and fiscal year from the same book-entries.list call, under a per-daybook lock (race risk; may clash with the accountant's own numbering). Number null on purchases is not used, because what Horus stores for it is undocumented (H3). An entry stored without a number has no reconciliation key if the accountant edits it before confirming; requiring or assigning a number is the Chift decision C7.
- supplier_* without invoice_number: heuristic duplicate check (proposal, configurable per consumer): POST /book-entries.list (FolderId, DaybookId, fiscal-year months, Filter.CompanyId = partner); flag an entry with the same Date and CompanyDetail.TotalAmount (and the same reference once H9 confirms where the header Comment is returned). On a match, return 409 with the existing id, or create and log it, per Chift policy (C6). Skipped when the partner is about to be created.

7. Build the Horus body.
- Header: Type, Number, Date, DueDate, CompanyId, totals, PaymentReferences, PaymentMode, CurrencyCode/CurrencyRate, OverrideTaxAmounts=true (proposed decision 'VAT amounts as issued', C2), AllowUnbalanced=false.
- Comment (D3): '{reference}', '{reference} | {customer_memo}' or '| {customer_memo}'.
- Confirmed (D12): false in review mode (proposed default) and for 'draft'; true for 'posted' in direct mode.
- InvoiceLines with CostLines: percentages become amounts as a product of combinations across plans, rounded with the largest-remainder method so the cost lines sum exactly to BaseAmount (D8); rows rounding to 0.00 are dropped, and more than 100 rows per line (proposal) → 422. Analytic checks (inactive section, Mandatory schema, WithAnalytics) run here, before any write.
- Append an invoice_correction line when header and lines differ within the rounding tolerance (step 1).

8. Create. First, if step 4 needs a partner write (companies.new, or the opt-in companies.update), run it now, after every check above has passed. Then POST /invoices.sales.new (customer_*) or POST /invoices.purchases.new (supplier_*). Without a PDF, use application/json. With a PDF, use multipart/form-data: file = the base64-decoded bytes, body = the JSON as a plain text form field, including FileName with its extension. Error handling (Guide: Responses & errors):
- 400: never retry as-is. Map to Chift 400/422 and surface ErrorType and Details.
- 404: map to Chift 404.
- 401: refresh once under the lock and retry. If the refresh fails, mark the connection disconnected.
- 403: map to Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details (D7). In direct mode it may also mean that the user cannot confirm entries (undocumented).
- 500 or timeout: before any retry, re-run the step-6 DocumentNo pre-check (D12), because Horus has no idempotency key and no invoice delete; retry with exponential backoff only if nothing is found. Never auto-retry a create sent without a number (Number=0): return an 'outcome unknown' error (code per C6); for a supplier invoice, run the step-6 heuristic check first, then surface the error. Calls with the same (folder, daybook, number) are serialised by a connector-side lock (proposal). Best effort only: whether a timed-out request can still be committed, and whether a new entry is listed at once, is undocumented (H3).
- If Horus rejects the invoice after a partner was created or re-flagged, return the partner Id in the error detail (it can be reused as partner_id). Partners are not rolled back, because Horus has no company delete endpoint.
9. If ignore_accounting_id=true: return the echoed request plus id = the Horus Id right away. Horus is synchronous, so the Id is already known.

10. Otherwise, read back with GET /book-entries.info?Id=<Id>: one call by Id, with no FolderId, DaybookId or period. Check Data.Folder.Id = folder_id (D13). It gives DocumentNo, Confirmed, Date, LastModifiedDate (last_updated_on), CompanyDetail (Company, DueDate, TotalAmount, TurnoverAmount, TaxAmount, RemarkPayment), Daybook and Document. Its CompanyDetail amounts are assumed EUR (D4) and are never returned under a foreign currency code. Add POST /account-histories.list (FolderId, the fiscal-year period, Filter.BookEntryId=Id, IncludeVatDetail, IncludeCostDetail, IncludeCompanyDetail, optionally Include='CompanyDetail.Company') only when a field needs line data: the EUR partner-line amount and applied CurrencyRate of a foreign-currency invoice, the partner collective account, or booked VAT/cost detail. If that list returns nothing, fall back to GET /account-histories.info for each AccountHistories[].Id from book-entries.info. Optionally call GET /documents.info with Document.Id for the file name. If the read-back fails, never re-create the invoice: return the Id with echoed values.

11. Assemble InvoiceItemOutMultiAnalyticPlans from the request echo, the resolved Ids and the read-back values (see the response mappings). Currency rule (D4): amounts are the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency; accounting_info.main_currency_total = the EUR partner-line amount; EUR amounts are never paired with a foreign currency code.

field_mappings.rule: Proposal (decision owner: Chift, C1; D12). Facts: entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, 'which lets the accountant review them in Horus Office before confirming them' (Guide: Data model); Confirmed=true is accepted by the request schema; invoices cannot be deleted through the API. Horus Confirmed means confirmed by the accountant, while Chift 'posted' means 'posted (finalized) in the accounting system'; the sources do not equate them. Proposed rule: a posting mode chosen per connection at activation. Review mode (proposed default): every invoice is pushed with Confirmed=false, whatever the Chift status. Direct mode: 'posted' → Confirmed=true, 'draft' → Confirmed=false. Chift 'draft' then means Horus unconfirmed: booked in the ledger and included in default list reads, but not yet confirmed by the accountant. The response always reports the status actually stored ('draft' when Confirmed=false). The recommended flow is to call Create client/supplier first: Chift describes partner_info for tools where 'we cannot create a client/supplier by API', and Horus can (companies.new). (1) POST /companies.list (FolderId) with Filter.ExternalReference = account_number as sent, then an exact, same-folder post-filter (string filters are 'contains'); the guide recommends ExternalReference to 'find the company again reliably'. (2) If nothing is found, Filter.SearchKey = account_number as sent, with an exact, same-folder post-filter (SearchKey is unique within the folder). The code is never sanitised or truncated: a value that create_client's SearchKey rules would change is rejected with 422 (limits to confirm, H7). (3) Reuse a match only if its Name matches account_name (case, accents, spacing and punctuation ignored); on a mismatch, return 409 with the existing company id, or reuse and log a warning, per Chift policy (C8). Never reuse silently. (4) If the match lacks the role flag for the invoice side (IsCustomer for customer_*, IsSupplier for supplier_*), reject with 422 ('partner lacks the customer/supplier role; use client/supplier creation with force_merge'), unless Chift policy enables the flag update (companies.update with CompanyId + the flag only; null or omitted fields, never ""). (5) No match: create the company with companies.new using create_client's required-field rules (SearchKey = account_number), with ExternalReference = account_number when Chift confirms it is a third-party code (C8). The defaulted fields (IsVatLiable=false, folder language and country) are logged, and returned as warnings if Chift adds a warning channel (C3). field_mappings.rule: Horus has no VAT-code list endpoint and accepts no VAT code on write. The connector owns a VAT catalogue built from the Horus tax-combination files (the two spreadsheets linked from the invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new reference pages, downloaded 13 Oct 2026, appendix C), one list per folder Legislation (BE/LU) and direction, and exposes it through a folder-scoped Chift GET vat-codes with ONE canonical id grammar (D2), used identically for decoding here and for encoding in get_invoices. Sales: 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}', plus '-{TaxCountryCode}' for OSS rows (BE TaxOrigin 13; LU TaxOrigin 24, 26, 29), whose rate and country are supplied per transaction; example 'S-21-0-0'. Purchases: 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}', with 'x' for an unused component; example 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true'. Decoding: the id must exist in the folder's list for the invoice direction (otherwise 422) and carry the prefix of the invoice side (S- for customer_*, P- for supplier_*); its components fill TaxRate/TaxOrigin/TaxType (+ TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue for purchases, null for 'x'; + TaxCountryCode for OSS sales). The Chift scope nat/eu/int published in GET vat-codes follows TaxType 0/1/2. Horus VatCode is never accepted or returned as the Chift tax_code (D2): it is an output-only string whose meaning is undocumented (H1). Catalogue labels are taken from the files (TaxOrigin labels). Canonical rendering (D2): rates as whole numbers without decimals, as in the files; TaxConditionValue as in the invoices.purchases.new description ('true', 'false', '35', '50', '75', '85'); 'x' for an unused component; where the files give 'XX' (rate and country supplied per transaction), the id carries the actual rate and country, so such ids are accepted on write for any rate/country pair and cannot be listed exhaustively by GET vat-codes (proposal, C2). Published ids never change: catalogue updates add ids and never rename them.

field_mappings.rule: Each CostLine row amount = BaseAmount × product(pct/100) over the plans of that row. Rounding (D8): largest-remainder method on the per-line product allocation: floor every row to the cent, then give the remaining cents one by one to the rows with the largest fractional remainders, so the cost lines sum exactly to the line BaseAmount. Example: 0.10 split 33/33/34 gives 0.03/0.03/0.04. Ties between equal remainders go to plan order, then account id, so the result is deterministic. Combination rows whose rounded amount is 0.00 are dropped (the sum still equals BaseAmount; e.g. 0.10 over 27 combinations leaves 17 rows at 0.00). Rows per invoice line are capped (proposal: 100); above the cap, reject with 422 until Horus states a limit (H13). Round trip: a later invoice retrieval recomputes whole-number percentages from the booked amounts, so small lines can read back differently (0.10 sent as 33/33/34 is booked 0.03/0.03/0.04 and reads back as 30/30/40).

limitations.description: No VAT-code list endpoint appears among the 72 documented endpoints, and invoice lines take no VAT code. They need TaxRate + TaxOrigin + TaxType (+ TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue for purchases), and only the combinations in the Horus tax-combination files are valid (appendix C: one list per legislation BE/LU and direction). VatCode/VatHeading appear only as read-only output (account-histories VatDetail), and their meaning is undocumented; there, TaxCondition has an extra value '4 = Article' that the purchase input does not accept (enum[0, 1, 2, 3]). The LU files use TaxOrigin codes outside the reference enums (sales up to 35 vs 0–20; purchases 40–56 vs 0–39), and several codes carry different labels in the reference and in the files. Accounts carry VAT settings (VatRate/VatNat) that can help default or validate a decoded combination.
limitations.impact: Chift GET vat-codes must be emulated from a connector-maintained, folder-scoped catalogue with the canonical D2 id grammar (S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}[-{TaxCountryCode}] / P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}), and lines[].tax_code is decoded from it. The catalogue is built from the published spreadsheets and must be refreshed whenever Horus changes them; Horus must confirm that the files are current and which source is authoritative for the LU codes (H1). Read-side asymmetry: VatDetail has no TaxKind, so get_invoices returns tax_code = null for purchase combinations that differ only by TaxKind (D2); a purchase tax_code written here may not survive the round trip, unless VatCode proves to be stable and one-to-one with a combination (H1).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Invoice Number is numeric (Chift invoice_number is a string). Invoices have no AutoGenerateNumber field, unlike miscellaneous operations, banks and financials. No uniqueness constraint, idempotency key or external reference field is documented for invoices.
limitations.impact: Non-numeric invoice numbers (and numbers with leading zeros) are rejected. Horus cannot generate a missing invoice number: the proposed default pushes such invoices unconfirmed with Number 0 and returns them as draft (Chift decision C7); connector numbering (max+1, race risk) is an opt-in only. Idempotency is emulated, best effort, with a book-entries.list DocumentNo pre-check that returns 409; supplier invoices without a number get only a heuristic check (supplier, date, total), and a create without a number is never retried automatically.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: No dedicated field for reference (the supplier's invoice number on purchases). Header free text is limited to Comment and PaymentReferences.
limitations.impact: reference is merged into Comment with the D3 convention ('{reference} | {customer_memo}', or '| {customer_memo}' without reference), so later GET invoices cannot filter on it and can only parse it back from the header Comment, whose location on read is undocumented. Comment length limits are undocumented (?).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Several Chift inputs have no Horus field: force_financial_period, withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, start_date/end_date, delivery_date, payment_term_id, and line unit_price/quantity/unit_of_measure.
limitations.impact: These are either rejected with 422 (force_financial_period when it differs from the invoice month, withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split) or ignored and logged, not returned to the caller, because the Chift create response has no warnings field (accrual dates, payment term, quantity/price). delivery_date: accepted when absent or in the invoice month; in another month, rejected or accepted with the limitation that Horus books VAT by invoice date, per Chift (C3). Clients relying on these fields lose that data.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Horus analytics are amounts on joint cost-line combinations (CostLines[].Amount + Costs[] per schema), not per-plan percentages. A folder can have at most 8 cost schemas, and each cost history at most 8 cost sections. Schemas can be Mandatory or Free (CostSectionType 900).
limitations.impact: Percentages must be converted to amounts with largest-remainder cent rounding (D8). Several split plans require a Cartesian product, which assumes the plans are independent. A read-back cannot reproduce integer percentages exactly. Free schemas (CostSectionType 900) are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8), so their values cannot be posted through the connector.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Currency: EUR is implicit (null). Only 32 other ISO codes are accepted. The folder must be configured for currencies, and no API field exposes that setting. The CurrencyRate direction is undocumented, and so are the currency of the invoice amounts and the date of the default 'rate of the day' (invoice Date or posting date).
limitations.impact: Invoices in currencies outside the enum are rejected. A rate in the wrong direction would misstate EUR amounts, so validate with Horus before go-live. D4 assumption: account-history Debit/Credit and CompanyDetail amounts are in EUR, so the response pairs echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency and returns the EUR partner-line amount only as main_currency_total. Sending non-EUR amounts in the invoice currency is itself an assumption (H4).
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: Create returns only {Id} (Guide: Responses & errors). GET /book-entries.info reads the entry back by that Id with no period, but it returns entry-level data only: lines appear as references (AccountHistories: Type + Id), without amounts, VAT, cost detail, currency or account search keys. Line data comes from account-histories.list, which needs FolderId and mandatory period parameters, or from GET /account-histories.info at one call per line.
limitations.impact: In the common case, the full Chift response needs echoed values plus 1 read-back call by Id (last_updated_on, status, DocumentNo, header totals, document). The actual EUR totals of a foreign-currency invoice and the partner collective account still need a second, period-bounded call (0-1 extra).
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: invoices.*.update is a full replacement: it needs every creation-required field, returns a NEW book entry Id, and deletes the original attachment.
limitations.impact: Chift invoice ids do not survive Horus updates, for example a draft confirmed later through the API. Any later status change or correction means re-sending the full payload and the PDF, and the Chift id and attachments_info change. Clients storing ids must be warned. Horus recommends reconciling on daybook + entry number rather than the Id alone.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Credit notes use Type=1, but the sources do not say whether amounts must be positive, or whether a credit note may be posted into a 200/100 daybook (or an invoice into 250/150). The posting guide does not tie Type to a daybook type. The connector applies the D1 fallback (customer_refund 250 → 200, supplier_refund 150 → 100), which relies on that undocumented acceptance.
limitations.impact: A wrong sign or a refused daybook gives a Horus 400 or reversed postings. Credit notes posted into a 200/100 daybook are told apart on read by the partner-line sign, which D1 applies in folders without a credit-note daybook (get_invoices). Needs Horus confirmation before go-live. The sign policy for input amounts is a proposal (see the sign-policy edge case; C5, H2).

limitations.description: A single DueDate per invoice; no instalments.
limitations.impact: due_dates[] in the response always has exactly one element.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Accepted attachment types are documented for all upload routes, invoices.*.new multipart included: Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, .jpg/.jpeg/.png (F). No size limit is documented.
limitations.impact: The connector can reject unsupported types before calling, but it cannot pre-check size. Large files may fail with an undocumented error that must be surfaced.

limitations.description: Confirmed means confirmed by the accountant. API entries are unconfirmed by default precisely so the accountant can review them in Horus Office. The Chift default status is 'posted'.
limitations.impact: Mapping 'posted' to Confirmed=true would mark invoices as accountant-validated without review. D12 proposes a posting mode chosen per connection at activation: review (push unconfirmed; proposed default) or direct (Confirmed=true for 'posted'). Decision owner: Chift (C1). In review mode, read routes show these entries only when unposted entries are requested (for example outstanding items with unposted_allowed=true) until the accountant confirms them; in direct mode a confirmed invoice cannot be undone through the API, and a 403 is possible if the user may not confirm (undocumented).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Horus legislations are BE and LU only, and the TaxOrigin labels are Belgian/Luxembourgish tax categories (e.g. 'Prestation hors Belgique', 'Prestations hors Luxembourg').
limitations.impact: Non-BE/LU tax scenarios cannot be expressed, and NL-specific Chift fields have no meaning here. Each legislation has its own combination list, so the VAT-code catalogue is per folder.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: The API has no invoice delete or cancel endpoint. The only book-entry delete is book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.delete, which works only on unconfirmed miscellaneous operations created through the API.
limitations.impact: The connector cannot undo a wrongly pushed or duplicated invoice, or roll back a multi-step flow (e.g. a failed fallback PDF attach); the accountant must fix it in Horus Office. That is why the duplicate pre-check before any retry is critical. The connector can never produce Chift status 'cancelled'. A company created from partner_info is not rolled back either (no company delete endpoint).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: All requests, writes included, run against the license's real database. No sandbox environment is documented.
limitations.impact: Connector development, QA and certification must use a dedicated test license or test folder. Because invoices cannot be deleted, test invoices remain.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Neither the API reference nor the guides document pagination, rate limits or the ErrorType catalogue; the only ErrorType example is 'not_found'.
limitations.impact: Lookup volume (several list calls per folder) and throttling behaviour are unknown, and mapping Horus 400s precisely to Chift 409/422/404 depends on ErrorType values Horus must provide.

limitations.description: partner_info carries only account_number (no description in the Chift spec, read as the company SearchKey, D10) and account_name. Companies created from it have no VAT number, no address, IsVatLiable=false, and the folder's language and country.
limitations.impact: A wrong reading of account_number would create or reuse the wrong third party. Companies created this way need completing in Horus Office; calling Create client/supplier first is the reliable path. The lookup uses ExternalReference first, then the exact code as sent: a code that sanitising would change is rejected, because two codes differing only by removed characters could otherwise resolve to the same company; reuse requires a name match (409 or a logged warning on a mismatch, C8).
limitations.label: A

edge_cases.case: customer_refund or supplier_refund sent with negative amounts (Chift does not state the input sign)
edge_cases.handling: Normalise to absolute values and send Type=1. Reject mixed-sign lines that cannot be represented; send negative lines only once Horus confirms they are allowed.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Header totals ≠ sum of lines (rounding by the invoicing tool)
edge_cases.handling: Generate an invoice_correction line (Δ base and Δ tax, with the correction account and tax code). Without invoice_correction, reject 422, because Horus requires header = sum of lines.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: VAT computed at invoice level, so a line's tax_amount differs from base × rate by more than 1 cent
edge_cases.handling: Send OverrideTaxAmounts=true so Horus keeps the amounts provided. Otherwise Horus recalculates and only adapts within 1 cent.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Analytic split 33/33/34 on an amount that is not divisible
edge_cases.handling: Largest-remainder rounding on the per-line product allocation (D8): floor each row to the cent and give the remaining cents to the largest remainders (e.g. 0.10 → 0.03/0.03/0.04), so the CostLines sum exactly to BaseAmount.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Two plans each split, e.g. Dept A 50 / B 50 and Project X 30 / Y 70
edge_cases.handling: Four CostLines: A-X 15%, A-Y 35%, B-X 15%, B-Y 35% of BaseAmount (product, independence assumption). Document this behaviour for clients.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line without analytic_distribution while a cost schema is Mandatory, or folder WithAnalytics=false while a distribution is sent
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check against cost-schemas.list Mandatory and folders.info WithAnalytics, and reject with a clear message. Horus behaviour is otherwise undocumented.

edge_cases.case: More than 8 analytic plans, or a plan id that is not a Horus cost schema
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422. Horus allows at most 8 schemas per folder.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Timeout or Horus 500 on the create call
edge_cases.handling: Never retry blindly (D12): Horus has no idempotency key and no invoice delete. First re-run the book-entries.list pre-check on DaybookId + DocumentNo (+ CompanyId); unconfirmed entries are included by default. If found, return the existing entry or 409. Otherwise retry with exponential backoff (Guide: Responses & errors). For a draft with Number=0, duplicates cannot be detected reliably, so do not auto-retry; surface the error. GET /book-entries.info cannot replace the pre-check here, because a timed-out create returns no Id.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: invoice_number non-numeric, e.g. 'F2024-001'
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422, or strip it to digits only if Chift accepts that policy. The original string must not be appended freely to Comment, which is reserved for the D3 reference | customer_memo convention; it can be carried only as reference when reference is empty.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Posted sale invoice without invoice_number
edge_cases.handling: Compute max(DocumentNo)+1 for the daybook and fiscal year, or reject and require a number. This carries a race risk, and the Horus numbering pattern is unknown (examples 201909001 / 1904001 / 202409001).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: No journal_id and several daybooks of the D1 candidate type (e.g. two 200 daybooks for a customer_invoice, or no 250 and two 200 daybooks for a customer_refund)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 400 'journal_id required' (D1; Chift rule: "otherwise, an error will be thrown").
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: invoice_date in a closed period, a closed fiscal year, or outside any fiscal year
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check, as Horus recommends, with fiscal-years.list closure dates (LastSalesClosureDate/LastPurchasesClosureDate/LastVatClosureDate; IncludeFuture for future years) and fiscal-years.info IsClosed. Reject with an explicit message.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Currency not in the Horus CurrencyCode enum (e.g. AED)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422 before calling Horus (the enum is documented).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Foreign currency on a folder that is not configured for currencies
edge_cases.handling: No API field allows a pre-check. Expect a Horus 400 and pass its Details through (the exact Horus behaviour is undocumented).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: currency='EUR' with currency_exchange_rate=1
edge_cases.handling: CurrencyCode=null, CurrencyRate=null (null = EUR).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: PDF present but pdf_name missing or without an extension
edge_cases.handling: Default FileName to '<number>.pdf', or append '.pdf'; FileName with its extension is required when a document is attached.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Attachment that is not one of the supported types (e.g. .docx)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422 before calling. Supported types are Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, .jpg/.jpeg/.png. File size cannot be pre-checked because no limit is documented.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: PDF attached in a second call (fallback) fails after the entry was created
edge_cases.handling: Prefer the single multipart call. In the fallback, return the created id with attachments_info.status='no' plus a warning, or retry book-entries.documents.new (which fails if a document already exists). Before any retry, check GET /book-entries.info → Document: if it is not null, the first attach succeeded and must not be retried. The entry cannot be rolled back.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Partner exists but IsCustomer=false for a sale (or IsSupplier=false for a purchase)
edge_cases.handling: partner_info flow (D10): set the missing flag with companies.update (CompanyId + flag only, never "" values). partner_id flow: the same flag update is the closest consistent behaviour (or reject, per Chift policy). Whether Horus refuses an invoice for a company without the flag is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: OSS distance sale (TaxOrigin 13) without a country
edge_cases.handling: Under D2 an OSS sales code always carries its country (S-{TaxRate}-13-{TaxType}-{TaxCountryCode}), so TaxCountryCode comes from the code. An OSS id without the country component is not a catalogue id: reject 422. shipping_country is only a cross-check (warn when it differs).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Purchase on an account that requires a vehicle, or has a personal share (accounts HasPersonalShare)
edge_cases.handling: VehicleId and PersonalShare stay null because Chift has no source (an optional per-consumer default vehicle is possible). Whether Horus applies defaults or rejects is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: regroup_lines=true with different descriptions on merged lines
edge_cases.handling: Concatenate the descriptions (truncated). The response echoes the regrouped lines actually booked.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line-level read-back (account-histories.list) finds no lines because Horus booked a different accounting month than invoice_date
edge_cases.handling: The header read-back is unaffected, because GET /book-entries.info takes only the Id. For the account-histories.list add-on, query the whole fiscal year with Filter.BookEntryId. If it still returns nothing, fall back to GET /account-histories.info for each AccountHistories[].Id from book-entries.info, which needs no period.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Read-back on a folder that is not VAT liable or has no analytics module
edge_cases.handling: VatDetail comes back null when the folder is not VAT liable, and CostDetail null when the folder has no analytics. Fall back to the echoed values.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Analytic account maps to a cost section that is inactive or locked (IsLocked=true)
edge_cases.handling: Inactive sections are in the D8 cache (IncludeInactive = true) and are rejected with 422 'analytic account inactive'. For IsLocked sections, either reject or pass through and surface Horus's error; the behaviour is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: lines[].account_number is a summary (IsSummary=true) or collective account (e.g. 400000, IntCategory COLLECCUS)
edge_cases.handling: Pre-validate with accounts.list and reject with 422, since Chift requires a general account (assumption: Horus does not accept summary accounts on invoice lines).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Access token expires in the middle of the multi-call flow, or one consumer pushes several invoices in parallel
edge_cases.handling: Refresh proactively before expiry. On a 401, refresh once under a per-connection lock, persist the new pair before using it, then retry the failed call; for the create call, only after the DocumentNo pre-check. Parallel unserialised refreshes break the connection because refresh tokens are single-use.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: A company created from partner_info (IsVatLiable=false) is used with a reverse-charge or intra-EU tax combination (e.g. sales TaxOrigin 1 'Vente Cocontractant', TaxType 1 European)
edge_cases.handling: Warn, or reject when the decoded combination implies a VAT-liable counterparty. Recommend calling Create client/supplier with the VAT number first.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: companies.new in the partner_info flow hits an existing SearchKey that the exact-match post-filter missed (case difference, race)
edge_cases.handling: Expect a Horus 400. Re-query companies.list (exact SearchKey, same folder) and reuse the existing company, setting its role flag with companies.update if needed (D10). Duplicate-SearchKey behaviour is undocumented; only duplicate VAT numbers are documented as refused by default.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Connector testing and certification
edge_cases.handling: Run every .new call against a dedicated test license or test folder. Requests hit the license's real database, and test invoices cannot be deleted.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: An invoice was pushed by mistake or twice
edge_cases.handling: No API delete exists for invoices. Report the duplicate to the client; the accountant must correct it in Horus Office.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Read-back fails after a successful create (GET /book-entries.info returns 404 or 500, or times out)
edge_cases.handling: Never re-create: the invoice exists, and Horus has no invoice delete. Return the Id with echoed values (last_updated_on null), log the failure, and retry the read-back later with backoff. A 404 right after a synchronous create is unexpected and should be reported to Horus.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: customer_refund (or supplier_refund) in a folder with no 250 (or 150) daybook
edge_cases.handling: D1 fallback: post with Type=1 into the single 200 (or 100) daybook. If Horus refuses a credit note in a Sale/Purchase daybook, surface the 400 and ask for a credit-note daybook or an explicit journal_id. get_invoices still finds the entry, because it scans both sibling daybook types and classifies each entry by the partner-line sign (D1).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: journal_id of a daybook from another folder, or with a Type outside the invoice side (e.g. a 600 or a 100 daybook for a customer_invoice)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 400: the id is not in the folder's cached daybooks.list, or GET /daybooks.info → Data.Folder.Id ≠ folder_id (D13), or the Type is not 200/250 (customer_*) / 100/150 (supplier_*).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: partner_id of a company in another folder of the same license
edge_cases.handling: GET /companies.info → Data.Folder.Id ≠ folder_id → reject 400 before creating (D13). Horus's own behaviour on a cross-folder CompanyId is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Analytic plan is a Free schema (CostSectionType 900), or a Free schema is Mandatory in the folder
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422: Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8). If a Free schema is Mandatory, lines cannot satisfy it through the connector; what Horus does with a missing mandatory value is undocumented, so surface Horus's error and keep the open question.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Only customer_memo is set, or reference contains ' | '
edge_cases.handling: Memo only → Comment '| {customer_memo}' (D3); read routes must treat a leading '| ' as reference = null, because a split on ' | ' alone would not match it. A reference containing ' | ' would split wrongly on read: replace the separator inside the reference or reject it (connector policy).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Foreign-currency invoice created with ignore_accounting_id=true
edge_cases.handling: Return the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency (D4). main_currency_total = null, because the EUR partner-line amount needs a read-back. Never pair EUR amounts with the foreign code.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Company created from partner_info in a folder whose Language is 'XX'
edge_cases.handling: Send LanguageCode = 'XX' as-is (D9 write-side fallback). Whether companies.new accepts 'XX' on write is undocumented; on a Horus 400, surface the error.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: status = posted while the consumer has the 'always push unconfirmed' setting on
edge_cases.handling: Send Confirmed=false (D12) and return status 'draft', the actual Horus state, so the client is not told the entry is final.
edge_cases.label: D

open_questions.question: Can a credit note (Type 1) be posted into a 200/100 daybook, and an invoice into 250/150? For credit notes, must amounts be positive?
open_questions.why: The D1 auto-selection posts customer_refund into a 200 daybook (supplier_refund into 100) when the folder has no 250 (150) daybook. Neither the API reference nor the posting guide ties Type to a daybook type or states the sign.

open_questions.question: Is Number unique per daybook and fiscal year? Does invoices.*.new reject or flag a duplicate Number, and with which ErrorType? Is there an idempotency key or external reference for invoices, or a way to get the next free number of an invoice daybook? (AutoGenerateNumber exists only on miscellaneous operations, banks and financials. Documents expose Status '900: PossibleDuplicata' / '901: DuplicataNumber', which hints at duplicate detection on the document side only.)
open_questions.why: Needed for Chift's invoice_number idempotency and for auto-numbering of posted invoices.

open_questions.question: Please provide the accepted-combination files (Tax-combinations-sales.xlsx and Tax-combinations-purchases.xlsx). Is there an API endpoint, current or planned, that lists VAT codes or accepted tax combinations? Are the files versioned?
open_questions.why: The D2 synthetic VAT catalogue behind Chift GET vat-codes and lines[].tax_code is built from these files, which are not among the admissible sources.

open_questions.question: Direction and meaning of CurrencyRate (1 EUR = x CUR, or 1 CUR = x EUR); currency of CompanyDetail amounts (and of account-history Debit/Credit). Are invoices.*.new TotalAmount/BaseAmount/TaxAmount given in CurrencyCode or in EUR? (invoices.sales.outstanding.* return both TotalAmount and TotalCurrencyAmount, which suggests EUR versus invoice currency.) How can we detect that a folder 'allows currencies'?
open_questions.why: D4 assumes Debit/Credit and CompanyDetail amounts are EUR. Needed to map force_currency_exchange, currency_exchange_rate and the amounts correctly, and to compute main_currency_total.

open_questions.question: Does Horus derive the accounting period (AccountingMonth/AccountingYear) from Date, and is there any way to force the period on invoice creation?
open_questions.why: Determines whether force_financial_period can ever be supported, and which period to query on read-back.

open_questions.question: With several cost schemas, must every CostLine carry one Costs entry per schema, only for Mandatory schemas, or can rows mix schemas? What value format applies to Free schemas (CostSectionType 900)? Are locked (IsLocked) cost sections refused on posting?
open_questions.why: Validates the percentage-to-joint-combination conversion for the multi-plan route, and decides whether Free schemas (excluded in v1 under D8) can be supported later.

open_questions.question: What size limit applies to the file in the multipart variant of invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new?
open_questions.why: File types are documented, but Chift accepts any base64 pdf, and we need to pre-validate size.

open_questions.question: What are the maximum lengths of Comment, PaymentReferences and the line Comment? Is PaymentReferences validated as a Belgian structured communication?
open_questions.why: The D3 convention concatenates reference and customer_memo into the header Comment, so truncation rules must be defined.

open_questions.question: Please confirm that the 'Id' query parameter of GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info is the FolderId (deduced from the guide, which requires FolderId).
open_questions.why: Needed if this endpoint is used as a sales read-back. The deduction is strong but not stated.

open_questions.question: What are the rate limits, and do list endpoints paginate or truncate large results?
open_questions.why: Neither the API reference nor the guides (Making requests, Responses & errors) document pagination or rate limits, and list responses show no paging fields. Each invoice triggers 2-4 calls when the cache is warm, and lookups rely on list endpoints.

open_questions.question: GET /book-entries.info documents only the Id parameter: does it really need no FolderId? For a foreign-currency invoice, in which currency are CompanyDetail.TotalAmount/TurnoverAmount/TaxAmount expressed? Is TurnoverAmount the invoice's BaseAmount? What format does CompanyDetail.DueDate use (typed string, unlike Date)? Is sideloading planned for this endpoint?
open_questions.why: book-entries.info is now the default read-back. These answers decide which response fields it can fill reliably, and whether the period-bounded account-histories.list call can be dropped for foreign-currency invoices.

open_questions.question: Which ErrorType values can invoices.*.new return (duplicate number, closed period, invalid tax combination, unknown account/cost section, currency not allowed, missing vehicle)?
open_questions.why: Only the example 'not_found' is documented. Precise mapping to Chift 404/409/422 depends on it.

open_questions.question: When the accountant confirms or edits an API-created invoice in Horus Office, does the book entry keep its Id? Is an invoice delete/cancel endpoint planned?
open_questions.why: Chift invoice ids must stay stable, and the API offers no way to roll back an invoice.

open_questions.question: What happens when VehicleId is missing on a purchase line whose account requires a vehicle, and when companies.new receives a SearchKey that already exists?
open_questions.why: Chift has no vehicle source, and the partner_info flow can collide on SearchKey. Both behaviours are undocumented.

open_questions.question: What sign convention does Chift expect on input for customer_refund and supplier_refund amounts?
open_questions.why: The request schema does not state it, and Horus has a separate Type flag.

open_questions.question: Is it acceptable to reject non-numeric invoice_number values? When the duplicate pre-check finds a match, should the connector return 409 or the existing invoice?
open_questions.why: The Chift idempotency guide was not provided.

open_questions.question: Is a connector-maintained synthetic VAT-code catalogue acceptable for GET vat-codes on a target with no VAT-code entity?
open_questions.why: It is the only way to satisfy the required lines[].tax_code.

open_questions.question: For unsupported optional inputs (withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, start/end_date, delivery_date, force_financial_period), should the connector reject them or ignore them with a warning?
open_questions.why: This is a product policy: it trades silent data loss against integration friction.

open_questions.question: For analytics, is the Cartesian-product (independence) conversion from per-plan percentages acceptable for multi-plan splits?
open_questions.why: Horus needs joint combinations; Chift provides only marginal splits per plan.

open_questions.question: Which default fits fiduciary clients for status 'posted': Confirmed=true, or the per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting switched on by default (D12)? Horus's view on API-confirmed entries would inform it.
open_questions.why: It is a business decision with an accounting-control impact for fiduciary clients.

open_questions.question: Is the PaymentMode enum value (as a string) acceptable as the id for GET payment-methods and payment_method_id? (Analytic ids are fixed by D8 as cost schema / cost section GUIDs.)
open_questions.why: The TRANSFORM rule for payment_method_id and due_dates[].payment_method_id depends on that choice.

open_questions.question: Can TaxKind be exposed on read (account-histories VatDetail)? What does the read-side TaxCondition value '4 = Article' mean, given that purchase input accepts only enum[0, 1, 2, 3]?
open_questions.why: Without TaxKind on read, get_invoices cannot re-encode some D2 purchase tax codes written by this route (tax_code returns null), so the create → read round trip loses the VAT code.

open_questions.question: Where does the invoice header Comment surface on read (partner-line Comment, RemarkCompany, Remark)?
open_questions.why: reference and customer_memo are stored in the header Comment (D3); get_invoices and outstandings can only return them if they know where to read it back.

open_questions.question: Does invoices.*.new refuse a CompanyId whose IsCustomer (sales) or IsSupplier (purchases) flag is false, or a CompanyId from another folder? Does companies.new accept LanguageCode 'XX'?
open_questions.why: Decides whether the D10 companies.update flag step and the D13 companies.info folder guard are mandatory or defensive, and whether the D9 folder-language fallback can fail.

open_questions.question: What does partner_info.account_number mean: a third-party code or a ledger account?
open_questions.why: The Chift spec gives no description. The connector treats it as the Horus company SearchKey (D10); if it is the collective ledger account (e.g. 400000), the find-or-create logic is wrong.

evidence_gaps: Pagination, rate limits and the ErrorType catalogue are documented nowhere: not in the API reference and not in any of the 15 guides. The only ErrorType example is 'not_found'.

The Tax-combinations-sales.xlsx and Tax-combinations-purchases.xlsx reference files linked from invoices.*.new and from the posting guide were not provided, so the D2 VAT catalogue (accepted rate/origin/type/kind/condition tuples) cannot be built from admissible sources.

GET /book-entries.info is now documented (Id query parameter; response identical to a book-entries.list item). Still undocumented: whether a FolderId is needed, the format of CompanyDetail.DueDate (typed string, unlike Date), the currency of the CompanyDetail amounts on foreign-currency invoices, whether TurnoverAmount equals the invoice BaseAmount, and sideloading support (not on the guide's list).

ba_insights: In Horus, an 'invoice' is a façade over a book entry. invoices.*.new 'will then be converted into a book entry' and returns only the book entry Id. That Id must be the Chift invoice id everywhere (GET invoices, GET attachments document_id). Any update generates a NEW Id and deletes the attachment, so Horus itself advises reconciling on daybook + entry number.

Terminology map, established from the Horus docs:
- **Horus folder = Chift folder:** the accounting record of one company; one license holds many folders.
- **Horus company = Chift client/supplier:** one entity with IsCustomer/IsSupplier flags.
- **Daybook = journal:** its Type drives which endpoint you post to; it has a SearchKey such as VEN.
- **Account:** a ledger account referenced by its search key.
- **Cost schema = analytic plan; cost section = analytic account.**
- **Confirmed:** validated by the accountant.
- **MatchNo:** the matching (lettering) number, NOT the invoice number, so matching.next-number.* must never be used for invoice numbering.

Why multi-call: Horus's own posting guide lists four prerequisites before posting an invoice: FolderId, the DaybookId of a 200/250 or 100/150 daybook, the CompanyId 'found or created', and the account search keys. One Chift call therefore becomes 1 create, 1 duplicate pre-check (whenever invoice_number is supplied, D12) and 0-2 read-back calls per invoice (usually just GET /book-entries.info by Id), plus reference lookups cached per folder (daybooks, accounts, the D8 analytics cache, fiscal years) and a cached companies.info folder guard per partner (D13). With a warm cache that is 2-3 Horus calls per invoice, 4 when line-level data is needed, and 1-2 more on the first invoice for a partner_info company (companies.list, then companies.update or companies.new).

Biggest trap: VAT. Chift assumes the target has VAT-code records with ids. Horus has none: it expects a combination of enums (rate + origin + type, plus kind/condition/value for purchases) checked against external tables. The connector must own a synthetic VAT-code catalogue with one id grammar shared by GET vat-codes, this route and get_invoices (D2): 'S-21-0-0' for a national 21% sale, 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true' for a deductible 21% purchase of merchandise. That makes GET vat-codes a hard dependency of invoice creation even though it is not in the case's list.

Second trap: analytics. Chift sends independent per-plan percentages. Horus stores amount rows that each combine one section per schema, i.e. a joint distribution. One plan converts exactly. Several split plans need a product, which assumes independence. Rounding uses the largest-remainder method so the cost lines sum exactly to the line's BaseAmount (D8). Chift ids are cost schema / cost section GUIDs, resolved to search keys from one per-folder cache that includes inactive sections, and Free schemas are out of scope in v1 (D8).

Numbering, idempotency and retries: Horus Number is numeric and required for sales ('can be 0 if not confirmed'). Invoices have no auto-number flag, Horus documents no uniqueness or external key, and there is NO invoice delete. Chift's recommended idempotency on invoice_number must therefore be emulated with a book-entries.list DocumentNo pre-check whenever invoice_number is supplied, surfaced as 409 (D12). The same pre-check must run before any retry after a 500 or timeout, because a duplicate cannot be undone through the API.

Status mapping is technically trivial (posted → Confirmed=true) but has documented business weight. Horus keeps API entries unconfirmed by default 'which lets the accountant review them'. D12 keeps posted → Confirmed=true but adds a per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting, recommended for fiduciary clients; the response then says 'draft'. Which default to ship is a product decision to agree with Chift and Horus.

Use the multipart variant whenever a PDF is present: the invoice and its document are created in one call. File types are documented (Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, jpg/jpeg/png); size is not. The two-step fallback (JSON create, then book-entries.documents.new) can leave an entry without its PDF, and that cannot be rolled back.

Sales and purchases differ even though one Chift route covers both. Purchases add TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue (deductibility), VehicleId and PersonalShare, and Number is nullable. Sales add TaxCountryCode for OSS. The tax-code decoder and validation must branch on invoice_type.

Response strategy: most of InvoiceItemOutMultiAnalyticPlans can be echoed from the validated request plus the resolved ids (partner, daybook). Pick the cheapest correct source per field. GET /book-entries.info, one call by Id with no period (folder-checked, D13), gives last_updated_on, status, DocumentNo (needed when a purchase was sent without a number), header totals and the document link. Currency (D4): amounts are the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency, and EUR amounts (CompanyDetail, Debit/Credit) are never paired with a foreign code. Only the EUR partner-line amount (main_currency_total) of a foreign-currency invoice, the partner collective account and booked line VAT/cost detail need the period-bounded account-histories.list (Filter.BookEntryId over the fiscal year), so add it only when one of those is required. Skip all read-backs when ignore_accounting_id=true; Horus is synchronous, so the id is still returned.

Operational hygiene from the guides:
- Refresh tokens are single-use, so serialise refreshes per connection and persist the new pair before use.
- Handle errors as Horus prescribes: 401 → refresh once and retry; 400 → do not retry, surface Details; 500 → back off.
- Send gzip.
- Ignore unknown response properties, because Horus adds properties without notice.
- Test only on a test license or folder, because the API works on real data.

Horus is BE/LU only (Legislation enum). That explains why nl_payment_terms_split and withholding_tax have no counterpart, and why the TaxOrigin labels are Belgian/Luxembourgish categories. Present these as market-scope limitations, not connector gaps.

Write for the round trip (D1, D2, D3): what this route writes must be readable by get_invoices. Refunds that fall back to a 200/100 daybook are still found, because get_invoices scans both sibling daybook types and classifies each entry by the partner-line sign. The D2 grammar lets get_invoices re-encode tax codes from VatDetail (except purchase codes that differ only by TaxKind, which read back as null). The D3 Comment convention ('{reference} | {customer_memo}') lets reference and customer_memo be parsed back, once Horus confirms where the header Comment surfaces on read.

partner_info is a Chift field without a description (D10). The connector reads account_number as the Horus company SearchKey and runs find → set role flag → create, never overwriting other company fields (companies.update with null, not "", for everything except the flag). Present it to clients as a convenience fallback: the reliable path is Create client/supplier first, then partner_id.

Folder scoping (D7, D13): one Horus license holds many folders and Id-only calls carry no FolderId. folder_id is required as soon as the connection has more than one selected folder, and every Id-only lookup (companies.info, daybooks.info, book-entries.info) checks Data.Folder.Id, so an id from another folder can never be posted or returned by mistake.
